title: Unify ingest-path accounting and rate-limiter provenance across HTTP/WS/gRPC
creator: Lena Wong
description: Several customers and internal audits surfaced small but persistent mismatches between billed token usage and observed rate-limiter decisions when requests flow through different ingress paths (REST HTTP, WebSocket streaming, and gRPC multiplexers). Root causes include divergent pretokenization length heuristics, inconsistent header-derived provenance (which affects tenant-level rate-pegging), and transient provisional accounting for streaming chunks that are never finalized. This ticket aims to unify the ingest normalization, attach stable provenance metadata to rate-limiter decisions, and add commit/rollback hooks for provisional streaming credits so accounting and rate limiting are deterministic and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: All ingest paths (HTTP POST, WebSocket frames, gRPC) produce identical pretokenization length for the same logical payload within 1 token variance across language-edge encodings
Rate limiter emits a provenance tag (ingest_path, client_id, idempotency_token) with every decision and logs an immutable decision id to the usage ledger
Provisional streaming credits are either committed or rolled back with clear events; no outstanding provisional credits remain after 60s of stream termination
End-to-end test harness reproduces previously observed discrepancy scenarios and shows token-accounting parity between replayed logs and final ledger
No customer-visible billing deltas after canary rollout; shadow mode shows <0.01% discrepancy under mixed workload
design_notes: Introduce canonical pretokenization module in front of all ingress adaptors so token length computation is identical; this module exposes a deterministic encoding and normalization (NFC unicode, trim optional trailing newlines, standardize CRLF -> LF) and uses the same tokenizer version as downstream accounting
Add X-Redwood-Ingest-Path and X-Redwood-Idempotency hints for client/proxy to pass through; fallback to server-derived fingerprint when missing
Rate limiter to attach a small (8 byte) decision UUID to decisions; this UUID is propagated into the ledger entries and logs to allow cross-checking decisions vs charges

Streaming credit lifecycle: on stream chunk receipt, allocate provisional_credit with a provisional_id; on terminal event (EOS/close), emit commit(provisional_id) which atomically moves provisional_credit to final ledger entry; on abrupt disconnect after grace window, emit rollback(provisional_id)

Backward compatibility: when ingestors do not support new headers, server will synthesize provenance based on connection meta (remote_addr, tls_fingerprint) but mark provenance as synthesized; billing/alerts will flag high rate of synthesized provenance for operators
Observability: emit metrics rate_limiter.decision.count_by_provenance and meter.delta.discrepancy.per_session; include debug traces mapping decision_uuid -> ledger_entry_id
Security: provenance headers must be validated and only accepted from trusted proxies; untrusted inbound must be rejected or sanitized
tasks: Spike: implement canonical pretokenization library and add cross-path unit tests (owner: Miguel)
Extend ingress adaptors (HTTP, WS, gRPC) to call canonicalizer and attach provenance headers (owner: Priya Shah)
Change rate limiter to emit decision_uuid and include provenance in logs/metrics (owner: Darius Kim)
Implement provisional_credit lifecycle in metering service and ledger adapter (owner: Elena Garcia)
Add e2e replay test harness that consumes saved request traces and validates final ledger parity (owner: SRE team)
Create canary plan: shadow-mode traffic on dedicated canary deployment for 72h, compare ledger differences and monitor alerts (owner: Miguel)
Docs: update billing doc and migration notes with new provenance semantics and headers (owner: Docs)
QA: fuzz streaming disconnect scenarios and verify rollback behavior (owner: QA)
Rollout: gradual enable by region with monitoring alerts gating full rollout (owner: Infra)
Postmortem template: capture any residual mismatches and corrective actions (owner: product)
comments: 2026-03-14 Lena Wong: Triage summary — this combines several customer complaints and internal audit samples. Prioritized P1 due to potential billing disputes. Assigned Miguel to lead implementation and coordinate with infra/SRE.

2026-03-15 Miguel Torres: Completed spike. Canonical pretokenizer prototype yields identical results for our regression corpus across HTTP and WS; gRPC showed a minor variance for CRLF handling which was fixed by normalizing newlines. Pushed branch runtime/canonical-pretokenizer.

2026-03-15 Priya Shah: Updated HTTP and WS adaptors to call the canonicalizer. Found an edgecase where proxy truncated long metadata headers — added header length sanitization and fallback provenance fingerprint.
2026-03-15 Darius Kim: Rate limiter now emits decision_uuid in local dev; integrating with logging pipeline. Need to coordinate with ledger adapter to persist decision_uuid in final entries.

2026-03-15 Elena Garcia: Ledger changes for provisional_credit are staged. Decided to use an explicit commit/rollback event model rather than time-based reconciliation to avoid retroactive charge adjustments.

2026-03-15 QA: Wrote fuzz tests for stream disconnects; initial run found a case where provisional credit was orphaned when client sent duplicate EOS frames. Adding idempotency guard on provisional commit.

2026-03-15 SRE: Preparing canary nodes. Will run shadow-mode for 48h before opening to limited customer cohort. Monitoring dashboard draft: metering/provisional_orphans, rate_limiter.provenance_synthesized_rate.
2026-03-15 Product review (Lena Wong): Request to add acceptance criteria around customer-visible dispute window; added additional criterion to avoid billing deltas during canary.
